lines: Welcome! Today we are talking about food words in Spanish.
First, fish. El pez is a fish alive in the water, but el pescado is the same animal once it has been caught and put on a plate. Ask a waiter for pez and you have technically ordered an aquarium.
Four common meats on Spanish menus: pollo, chicken; cerdo, pork; cordero, lamb; and carne de res, beef, the usual term in Mexico and much of Latin America.
Careful with ternera: in Mexico it is veal, the meat of a young calf, but in Spain it is the usual word for beef, young beef. Meat from an older animal is sold as vaca or buey.
The Spanish pantry runs on aceite de oliva and sal: la paella lleva mucho aceite de oliva. Spain is the world’s largest olive oil producer. The two basic starches are pan, bread, and arroz, rice.
Verduras covers vegetables broadly, while legumbres, lentils, chickpeas and beans, get a word of their own.
And fruta means fruit.
For example, a menu might list pollo, cerdo and pescado with arroz and verduras.
Do not mix up pez and pescado when you order, that is the trap.
Quick check: what do legumbres mean?
